explain.say: Put your hand on your chest. Can you feel your heart going thump, thump, thump, nice and steady? Music has a heartbeat too! Look at the board: on one side the pulse, on the other side the rhythm. Let us feel both.

explain.say: Look at the pulse side. The pulse is the steady beat that keeps going all through a song, every beat the same length. It is what you tap your foot or march to. Try it: tap, tap, tap, tap. Can you keep it steady?

explain.say: Now the rhythm side. Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds, usually following the words. Say juicy mangoes, juicy mangoes, and clap each part of the words. Did your claps come fast and slow, not all the same?

explain.say: Here is an easy way to find a rhythm: clap the syllables, the beats inside a word. Look at the board: wa, ter, mel, on. Four claps for watermelon! How many claps would your own name have?

Brilliant! The pulse stays steady while the rhythm dances on top, like a tabla player in India or a samba drummer in Brazil playing patterns over a steady beat. Wow fact: many dance songs have a pulse of about 120 beats a minute. Challenge: march the pulse with your feet while you clap watermelon with your hands!

faq.q: What is a pulse in music?
faq.a: The pulse is the steady beat that runs through a piece of music, like a heartbeat. Every beat is the same length, and it is what you march, tap or dance to.
asks: What is the beat in music?

faq.a: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds in music. It often follows the words of a song and changes as the song goes on.
asks: How do I clap a rhythm?

faq.q: What is the difference between pulse and rhythm?
faq.a: The pulse is steady and never changes its pattern; the rhythm is the mix of long and short sounds played on top of it.
asks: Is the beat the same as the rhythm?

faq.a: Tempo is how fast the pulse goes, measured in beats per minute. A slow lullaby might be 60 beats a minute and a lively dance 120 or more.

faq.q: How can I practise pulse and rhythm?
faq.a: Tap a steady pulse with your foot while clapping the rhythm of words or a song with your hands. Start slowly and speed up when it feels easy.
asks: How do I keep a steady beat?

facts: Tempo is measured in beats per minute (BPM).
A resting heart in an adult usually beats between 60 and 100 times a minute.

quiz.say: You tap your foot steadily to a song. What are you tapping?
quiz.show: A steady foot tap follows the…
quiz.why: The pulse is the steady beat that stays the same.

wrong.1: The rhythm has long and short sounds, so it is not steady.
wrong.2: The words follow the rhythm, not the steady beat.

quiz.say: How many syllable claps does the word banana have?
quiz.why: Ba, na, na: three syllables, three claps.

wrong.1: Say it slowly: ba, na, na is three parts.
wrong.2: Six is the number of letters, not syllables.
